blocks.text: Multiplication of two vectors is an important algebraic operation in vector algebra. This algebraic operation plays a fundamental role for understanding various physical and mathematical real-life situation. Unlike the multiplication of numbers, product of vector can be performed in two distinct ways. The two primary types of vector multiplication are the dot product and the cross product. The dot product is a scalar number while cross product is a vector quantity.

The paragraph above is printed just before the heading 14.2 (after Exercise 14.1). The heading 14.2 Dot or Scalar Product is then followed straight away by 14.2.1. The notes, map and lists below are our teaching: a short guide to the whole section.

blocks.title: Teaching note
blocks.text:
What is the dot product? It is a way of multiplying two vectors whose answer is a single number (a scalar), not a vector. For two vectors \(\underline{u}\) and \(\underline{v}\) with angle \(\theta\) between them:
\[\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = |\underline{u}||\underline{v}|\cos\theta\]
The number tells us how much the two vectors point the same way: it is positive when the angle is acute, zero when they are perpendicular, and negative when the angle is obtuse.
Why we need it: it gives the angle between two vectors, tests whether two vectors are perpendicular, gives the projection of one vector on another, and measures the work done by a force.

rows: Definition of \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v}\) by the angle and by components; Example 5
Projection of one vector along another: \(\frac{\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v}}{|\underline{u}|}\)
Work done by a constant force: \(W = \underline{F} \cdot \underline{d}\); Example 14

blocks.title: Key points
blocks.text:
1. The dot product of two vectors is a scalar (a number).
2. Two formulas give the same number: \(|\underline{u}||\underline{v}|\cos\theta\) (by the angle) and \(a_{1}a_{2} + b_{1}b_{2} + c_{1}c_{2}\) (by components).
3. Its sign shows the type of angle: positive for acute, zero for a right angle, negative for obtuse.

blocks.title: Common mistake
blocks.text: Writing the dot product of two vectors as a vector, e.g. \(\underline{u} \cdot \underline{v} = 2\underline{i} + 3\underline{j}\). The answer of a dot product never contains \(\underline{i}\), \(\underline{j}\) or \(\underline{k}\); it is just a number.
